thread:
dmitri: quick heads-up — after landing the recent fused-attn epilogue change, we see a regression on long-context workloads (~8k). ~10-15% slower end-to-end when KV cache is hot. anyone looked into qkv layout effects?

carol: I noticed this in nightly too. perf profiles point to higher L2 traffic inside the fused kernel when KV pages are active.

ben: more context — is this across all FlashAttention variants or only the fused path we added for epilogue fusion?

dmitri: seems isolated to the new fused kernel (the one that folds bias+rope into attention compute). vanilla flash variants are fine.

perfbot: perf-alert: fused-attn-epilogue v2 landed -> regression detected on test-suite/longseq (8k). +12% median latency vs canary. Profiling artifacts attached.

alice: hypothesis: QKV packing reorder increases stores to intermediate buffers which prevents effective KV paging (more full-warp spills). Could also be alignment changes that blow vector loads.

maria: I reproduced with a micro-bench: single-GPU, pax 8k, batch=1. When KV-cache enabled (paged mode) the fused kernel spends ~30% more cycles on global load/store. Without KV (no past) the kernel is same or slightly faster.

ben: can you paste the micro-bench numbers?

maria: ```
# micro-bench (8k seq, batch=1, A100)
baseline (flashattn-split): 121 ms
fused-epilogue: 136 ms (+12.4%)
KV disabled: fused-epilogue 119 ms
L2 read bytes (fused w/ KV): +22%
DRAM read bytes (fused w/ KV): +8%
```

carol: interesting that KV disabled makes fused faster than baseline. means the extra work is only problematic when the kernel touches large KV pages.

alice: could be a codegen ordering issue: we fused bias/rope into inner loops which now references KV entries in a non-streaming pattern. If the fusion introduces non-linear access across heads, we can lose locality.

dmitri: whether QKV packing layout changed? The fused kernel expects packed qkv (heads-major contiguous) but the KV cache page allocator provides per-head pages. mismatch could cause strided loads.

ben: action: run kernel-chooser sweep with permutations: (1) packed qkv vs interleaved, (2) rope applied pre- or post- attention, (3) bias fused vs separate. measure L2/DRAM and occupancy.

eva: FYI I rolled a quick patch that toggles a fast-path where we skip bias/rope fusion when KV cache size > threshold (config flag: fused_attn.skip_if_kv_large). Early numbers: reduces regression but loses small gain when KV absent.

carol: can we instead make fusion guarded by an access-pattern check? e.g., if stride between successive head loads > 1 cacheline, fall back. Might be expensive to compute at runtime though.

maria: another angle — batching heuristics: with long sequences and small batch, current batching groups N tokens into a single kernel call. Maybe batching increases working set; staggering small batches might reduce peak KV footprint. Need to test batcher changes too.

dmitri: yes — perf indicates working set peak is main driver. If we can change scheduling to prioritize locality (serve contiguous tokens from same sequence together) maybe fused kernel can keep L2 useful.

perfbot: recommended experiments (auto): run 3x parameter sweep: qkv_layout=[packed,interleaved], fusion=[on,off], batch_schedule=[seq-contiguous, round-robin]. Collect latency + L2 stats.

ben: I'll set up the sweep on perf-cluster (job queued). Maria, can you attach the nvprof traces for the fused path? we need PCNTL and memory op mix.

maria: uploaded nsight-export: /mnt/perf/artifacts/1795609876_fused_nsight.zip -> contains time-series of SM utilization and memory metrics. main takeaway: stalled waves waiting on L2 with high store utilization.

alice: that suggests the fused epilogue is doing more writes (maybe writing transient accumulators back to global). Do we materialize intermediate tensors when fusing? check temp buffer allocations.

carol: code pointer: src/runtime/kernels/fused_attention.cu: we introduced writeback of head_bias_accum when rope applied inline. Previously it was kept in regs and only reduced at end. Maybe the fusion forced stack spill.

dmitri: ok plan: (1) ben runs the sweep, (2) infra to run nsight on the failing config with larger L2 counter sampling, (3) alice to audit the fused kernel register pressure and see if we can lower spills, (4) eva to keep the skip-if-kv-large flag as a short-term mitigation behind a config toggle.

infra-bot: scheduled perf-sweep job: perf-sweep-1795609876 -> queue id 4821. ETA ~2h.

maria: one more datapoint — quantized path/8-bit kernels have smaller regression (only ~4%). likely because quant path reduces memory traffic per token. supports the memory-bound theory.

ben: if register pressure is the issue we can try rematerializing rope or bias from small LUTs instead of keeping big accumulators. also consider epilogue fusion variants that operate per-head to improve streaming.

dmitri: agree. prioritize low-effort mitigations first (config toggle). long-term aim for a fusion that preserves streaming-friendly access and low spill.

carol: assigning: ben (sweep + perf analysis), alice (kernel register audit), eva (toggle + canary deploy), maria (nsight traces + repro), dmitri (owner + follow-up). I'll open a tracking issue and link artifacts.

dmitri: thanks everyone. please drop any quick logs or weird findings here. ping @channel if we need more hands as perf-sweep results come in. :mag:
